content: A Creative Commons (CC) license is a type of public copyright license that allows the free distribution of a work that is otherwise protected by copyright. Authors use CC licenses when they want to grant others the ability to share, use, and build upon their work. These licenses provide authors with flexibility, such as permitting only non-commercial uses, and protect users from copyright infringement as long as they comply with the conditions specified in the license. There are various types of Creative Commons licenses, each with different combinations of conditions that govern the terms of distribution. The most current version of the license suite is 4.0. In October 2014, the Open Knowledge Foundation approved the CC BY, CC BY-SA, and CC0 licenses as conforming to the Open Definition for content and data. Works licensed under a Creative Commons license are subject to applicable copyright laws. This means CC licenses can be applied to any work that falls under copyright, such as books, plays, movies, music, articles, photographs, blogs, and websites. While software is also governed by copyright law and can use CC licenses, Creative Commons recommends using free and open-source software licenses instead. However, CC licenses can be used in specific cases, such as freeware models, as seen in examples like The White Chamber, Mari0, or AssaultCube. The Free Software Foundation also recommends CC0 as the preferred method for releasing software into the public domain. Creative Commons licenses do not alter rights granted by fair use or fair dealing, nor do they impose restrictions that violate copyright exceptions. These licenses are non-exclusive and irrevocable, meaning any work or copies obtained under a CC license can continue to be used under that license. If a work is protected by multiple CC licenses, the user may choose which license to follow. For a CC license to be valid, the author or licenser must hold exclusive rights to the work. The license is non-exclusive, royalty-free, and unrestricted in terms of territory and duration. It is irrevocable unless the author issues a new license after significant modifications to the work. Any use of the work outside the scope of copyright rules activates the public license. Once the license is activated, the licensee must comply with all conditions; failure to do so renders the agreement invalid and constitutes copyright infringement. The author or licenser retains the legal right to act on any infringement, and the licensee is given a limited period to correct non-compliance. Types of Creative Commons Licenses: 1. Attribution (CC BY): This license allows others to distribute, remix, adapt, and build upon the work, even for commercial purposes, as long as they credit the original creator. It is the most accommodating license, recommended for maximum dissemination and use of licensed materials. 2. Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA): This license permits others to remix, adapt, and build upon the work for any purpose, including commercial use, as long as they credit the creator and license their new creations under identical terms. It is often compared to copyleft licenses in free and open-source software. All derivative works will carry the same license, allowing commercial use. This license is used by Wikipedia and is recommended for materials that benefit from integration with Wikipedia or similar projects. 3. Attribution-NoDerivs (CC BY-ND): This license allows others to reuse the work for any purpose, including commercial use, but prohibits sharing the work in adapted form. Credit must be provided to the original creator. 4. Attribution-NonCommercial (CC BY-NC): This license allows others to remix, adapt, and build upon the work for non-commercial purposes. While new works must credit the creator and remain non-commercial, they do not need to be licensed under the same terms. 5. Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike (CC BY-NC-SA): This license permits others to remix, adapt, and build upon the work for non-commercial purposes, provided they credit the creator and license their new creations under identical terms. 6. Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs (CC BY-NC-ND): This is the most restrictive of the six main licenses. It only allows others to download the work and share it with others as long as they credit the creator. However, they cannot modify the work in any way or use it for commercial purposes.
